description: Correct post-signing verification which treats a DSSE envelope as its own artifact.

criteria.requirement: Post-signing verification of a DSSE bundle stops presenting the envelope's pre-authentication encoding as the artifact, so it is no longer compared against the subjects the envelope declares.
The change is confined to the DSSE case: a bundle carrying a message signature is still verified against the signed artifact bytes as before.
The bundle is still verified against the supplied trusted root before it is returned, and the signing API gains no new caller-supplied input to make that possible.
The code records why an artifact is deliberately not checked here: the caller supplied the envelope and the subjects it names, so this check has nothing independent to compare them against.
The candidate builds and vets the package it changes, makes a focused commit, and reports both accurately in relation to the trace and deterministic results.

The final response states what the post-signing check was comparing, why that comparison could never succeed for DSSE, what it does instead now, and what is deliberately no longer checked, in direct technical language.
